currentExpertConclusions.expertAnalysis: The requirement text for R-1-0012 describes activities that conserve tidal wetlands (protecting at-risk wetlands, improving water management, maintaining water quality, recharging sediment, creating accommodation space). This rule is located in Section 4 (Applicability Conditions) of the VM0007 v1.8 methodology framework. The supplied methodology excerpt from the derived rules.rich.json artifact (not verified against the official PDF) establishes that this applicability condition describes tidal wetland conservation activities under the WRC (Wetlands Restoration and Conservation) component of VM0007. The language is specific to tidal wetland environments — referencing water management, sediment recharge, and accommodation space — which are WRC concepts, not REDD/avoided-deforestation concepts. The Maya PDD evidence provided for this rule is limited to anti-discrimination text, which does not address tidal wetland conservation activities. No project evidence in the packet addresses tidal wetlands or establishes the project's activity type for R-1-0012 specifically. The applicability of this rule depends on whether the Maya project includes WRC components, which is not directly established by any evidence in the R-1-0012 candidate evidence. Without project evidence confirming the project's activity category or site characteristics, applicability cannot be definitively resolved from this packet alone. The anti-discrimination candidate evidence is irrelevant to this rule's applicability determination.

currentExpertConclusions.expertAnalysis: R-1-0013 requires baseline agents of wetland degradation to meet three criteria: (a) cause alteration in hydrology or loss of SOC, (b) have no documented legal right, and (c) have degraded wetlands in the historical reference period. This rule is located in Section 4 (Applicability Conditions) of VM0007 v1.8. The language is specific to wetland degradation agents — referencing hydrology alteration and SOC loss in wetlands — which is a WRC/CIW (Conservation and Improvement of Wetlands) concept, not a REDD/avoided-deforestation concept. The supplied methodology excerpt is from the derived rules.rich.json artifact (not verified against the official PDF). The Maya PDD candidate evidence includes the applicability table from the PDD, which states the project area contains no peatlands or tidal wetlands and categorizes baseline deforestation as planned deforestation (APDef). The methodology module selection table shows VMD0006 (BL-PL) for the planned deforestation baseline. These evidence items establish that the Maya project is a REDD/APDef project without WRC components. The wetland-agent criteria in this rule are structurally different from the deforestation-agent criteria in R-1-0003. The REDD context and the WRC context appear to be separate applicability branches within Section 4, but without the official VM0007 v1.8 publication, this structural separation cannot be confirmed with certainty.

currentExpertConclusions.expertAnalysis: R-2-0008 addresses carbon pool selection for REDD project activities under Section 5.3.2. The methodology requires: (1) HWP and dead wood must be included when they increase more or decrease less in the baseline than in the project scenario; (2) in all other cases, only aboveground biomass is mandatory; (3) symmetric accounting — inclusion in baseline implies inclusion in project and leakage; (4) T-SIG or Appendix 1 for significance testing. The supplied methodology excerpt (from derived rules.rich.json, not verified against the official PDF) establishes these criteria clearly. The candidate evidence from the Maya PDD states harvested wood products are excluded because they were deemed de minimis following VM0007's Appendix 1 significance testing, with reference to Appendix 22 for the calculation details. The evidence also states dead wood (identified as de minimis) was nonetheless included due to potential future hurricane/tropical storm increases. This directly addresses the conditional logic: the project performed Appendix 1 significance testing, found HWP insignificant (de minimis), and provided the test reference. Dead wood was conservatively included despite being de minimis. The HWP condition is triggered by the need to determine whether HWP increases more in the baseline scenario. The evidence states HWP are de minimis, which implies they do not trigger the mandatory inclusion condition, but the actual significance test results are not included. Table 4 is referenced in the methodology but not provided in the candidate evidence.

supportingMethodologyEvidence.quote:
5.3 Carbon Pools

5.3.1 General
Any significant decreases in carbon stock in the project scenario and any significant increases in carbon stock in the baseline scenario must be accounted for. In addition, decreases in the baseline scenario and increases in the project scenario can be accounted for. Where REDD activities take place on wetlands, the project must account for expected emissions from the soil organic carbon pool or change in the soil organic carbon pool in the project scenario, unless they are deemed de minimis. The significance of this pool may be determined by using the tool T-SIG or Appendix 1. Significance of pools must be determined ex-ante or at baseline reassessment for a specific baseline validity period, as well as at verification for a specific monitoring period.

Selection of carbon pools and the appropriate justification must be presented in PD and in the monitoring report (MR).

5.3.2 REDD

The carbon pools (and corresponding methodology modules) included in or excluded from the boundary of REDD project activities are shown in Table 4.

Harvested wood products and dead wood must be included when they increase more or decrease less in the baseline than in the project scenario. In all other cases, only aboveground biomass is mandatory. If a carbon pool is included in the baseline accounting, it must also be included in project scenario and leakage accounting.

Where the carbon pool in harvested wood products and dead wood increases more or decreases less in the baseline case than in the project case, the tool T-SIG or Appendix 1 must be used to determine whether significant. Insignificant pools can always be ignored.

supportingProjectEvidence.quote: The following carbon pools are accounted for: aboveground tree biomass (for trees with a diameter at breast height of greater than or equal to 5 cm), belowground tree biomass, aboveground biomass for palms, standing and lying dead wood, and soil organic carbon. Harvested wood products and CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 88 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 belowground palm biomass are excluded because they were deemed de minimis following the guidance provided in VM0007’s Appendix 1: Testing Significance of GHG Emissions. Appendix 21 includes information on how carbon stocks in the harvested wood product pool were estimated. Tab "Test of sig - 6 year bsl valid" of Appendix 22 provides the details of these significance testing calculations. Belowground palm carbon stocks are calculated the same way as belowground tree carbon stocks, the details of which are provided in section 3.2.1.2.1. While dead wood was also identified as de minimis, given the potential future increase in the size of this pool in the event of a hurricane or tropical storm, it was deemed important to include. All the included carbon pools are accounted for in the baseline and project scenarios as well as in the accounting of activity shifting leakage. Given the fact that harvested wood products are identified as de minimis, market effects leakage due to decreased timber harvest was also excluded from the analysis. Leaf litter, herbaceous vegetation, and lianas were not measured, which resulted in a conservative estimation of carbon stocks in the project area. The carbon stocks in post-deforestation agricultural biomass in the baseline scenario are also accounted for.
